title: Countries whose law names femicide or feminicide
note: Verified against ECLAC (November 2023: 18 Latin American countries) and the UN Women CSW70 expert paper by Patsili Toledo (December 2025: the same 18 plus Cyprus, Croatia, Malta, Italy; Belgium as a prevention and data law). CATW's brief puts the figure at roughly three dozen; the difference is most likely countries that treat gender motive as an aggravating circumstance without naming the crime (for example Spain, Turkey, Canada), which are not shown here.

sources.name: ECLAC Gender Equality Observatory, The obligation of States to prevent femicidal violence (November 2023)
ECLAC, Note for Equality No. 27: Femicide, the most extreme expression of violence against women
UN Women, Patsili Toledo Vasquez, Femicide/Feminicide and Access to Justice for Women and Girls, CSW70 expert paper (December 2025)
RTE, Croatia passes law making femicide a specific crime (March 2024)
University of Padua Human Rights Centre, Italian Parliament approves law introducing the crime of femicide, Law 181 of 2 December 2025
GCJ Network, Criminalising femicide: what the Western Balkans can learn (North Macedonia, Cyprus, Malta)
EIGE, Measuring femicide, intimate partner violence and rape: methodology and metadata for 13 indicators (2021)

countries.name: Sweden
countries.note: No femicide offence; the state counts femicides anyway. EIGE's 13 indicators give EU states uniform definitions of intimate partner violence, femicide and rape.

countries.name: Spain
countries.note: No femicide offence; a national system counts intimate partner and non-partner feminicide and children killed in the context of violence against their mothers (UN Women CSW70 paper, EIGE 2025).
